findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap on fallible I/O in production code
findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (permission denied, file not found, encoding error) panics the entire thread instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? operator

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — I/O (stdout) inside a data-loading function that should be pure calculation
findings.failure_mode: Side effects in core logic break determinism, make testing harder, and couple parsing to a concrete output destination
findings.fix: Remove println! from the core function. If logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell layer that calls this function

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on fallible parse in production code
findings.failure_mode: Any non-numeric or out-of-range value in the second column panics the thread instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Return Result and use ? on parse: parts[1].trim().parse::<u32>()? or handle with map_err

findings.problem: as u16 — lossy width-reducing cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: Values > 65535 silently truncate to u16::MAX (65535), producing incorrect data without any error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and return Result, or use checked_into and map_err on error

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec produced by split + collect
findings.failure_mode: A line with zero commas (single field) causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the None case; use .get(0) with ? or match

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into Vec produced by split + collect
findings.failure_mode: A line with exactly one comma (single field after delimiter) causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle missing second field with ? or explicit error

findings.problem: split(',') + collect() + indexing instead of split_once for simple two-field extraction
findings.failure_mode: Allocates a full Vec of Strings and splits all fields when only two are needed; unnecessary allocation and over-splitting for a fixed two-field line format
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(...) to extract exactly two fields without collecting into a Vec

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> directly instead of Result<Vec<Record>, E> — all fallible operations (read, parse, index) silently panic
findings.failure_mode: The API contract promises a Vec but can never actually return one on any error; callers have no way to distinguish success from unrecoverable failure
findings.fix: Change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, SessionLoadError> (or similar typed error enum) and propagate all fallible operations with ?

findings.problem: No try_reserve or bounded allocation strategy — Vec grows unbounded from file input
findings.failure_mode: Malformed or extremely large files can trigger excessive allocation and OOM without any bounds checking
findings.fix: Use Vec::with_capacity on a line-count estimate, or add a max-records guard. At minimum, use try_reserve with error handling before the loop.

findings.problem: Each line allocates a Vec<String> with .map().collect() when only two trimmed strings are needed
findings.failure_mode: Per-line heap allocations are unnecessary overhead for fixed two-field lines; allocates N Vec<String> objects for N lines
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') + .trim() + to_string() directly into Record fields without intermediate Vec allocation

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_sessions performance — no baseline command, no workload description, no target hardware specification
findings.failure_mode: Performance regressions go undetected; no evidence that the function meets any throughput or latency SLO
findings.fix: Add a Criterion or minitrace benchmark for load_sessions with a representative input file, specifying workload, hardware, and baseline metrics

findings.problem: No profiler evidence showing allocation hotspots in the split + collect path
findings.failure_mode: Cannot confirm whether per-line Vec<String> allocations are a real hotspot or a premature optimization concern
findings.fix: Run cargo-flamegraph or similar profiler on representative input to measure allocation profile

findings.problem: No second-ring evidence (assembly, allocation traces, SBOM) for the u32-to-u16 cast path or fs I/O path
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify whether the lossy cast compiles to expected instructions or whether fs read is the true bottleneck
findings.fix: Compile with cargo rustc -- -C opt-level=3 and inspect assembly with rust-objdump or similar; trace allocations with alloc-trace or valgrind

residual_risk: Static review identified 8 BLOCKER and 3 MAJOR findings across forbidden constructs, functional-core violations, unsafe parsing/access, and missing allocation discipline. No commands were executed during review. All unwrap() calls, lossy as casts, unchecked indexing, hidden I/O (println), and missing Result types must be repaired before any delivery. A typed error enum, Result return type, split_once-based parsing, checked conversion, and removal of println are the minimal fix set. Benchmark and profiler evidence must be added for any future performance claims.
